recommendation: Fund billing_support next quarter, starting with the free-tier restrictions issue, then pursue ad frequency as a related monetization-friction item and fix false connection errors/playback stops as a secondary track. Playback is the main alternative if severity is weighted over volume.
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation

**Priority area: billing/support.** Fund first: (1) free-tier restrictions on basic playback controls (ISS-billing-free_tier_restrictions), (2) review of ad frequency (ISS-usability-ads_frequency), which shares the free-user paywall theme, and (3) a smaller watch item on playback stops/skips (ISS-playback-stops_pauses_skips). The generic "general dissatisfaction" issue ranks first but names no actionable problem, so it is not fundable as is.

## Why

- Free-tier restrictions is the top specific issue: 701 complaints [C005], severity sum 2,082 [C008], mean severity 2.970043 [C007].
- The billing_support group has 882 complaints [T013], a severity sum of 2,570 [T014], and 169 cancellation-language records [T017], the most of any group. That is stated intent, not observed churn.
- Ads frequency adds 564 complaints [C009] with a priority score of 1,210 [C012].
- Trend: billing_support complaints rose from 107 [early window, 4.04% share] to 590 [late window, 13.04% share] across full months, and the late window had 4,525 completed records versus 2,649 early. Note the late-window total is larger.

Customer examples:
- "Doesn't even make sense to include basic features of the app into a premium subscription." [R:8f0b1f60-07bd-421e-a5c1-35a1b119ab78]
- "With the recent update, basic features (such as shuffle, looping, moving the song marker (rewind-forward) and more) have been disabled for free users." [R:4349285f-b3cf-43aa-b93e-e4bacaf7f56e]
- "Seems like I'm listening more ads than actual music." [R:2c33acbd-4776-4269-adb9-a3bc59845f9a]

## Alternatives considered

- **Playback:** 607 complaints [T019], severity sum 2,004 [T020], mean severity 3.301483 [T021], and 240 severe (4+) records [T022] versus 98 for billing_support [T016]. It is the most severe large group, and would take priority if leadership values severity over volume or if its late share rises. Its share fell from 7.02% to 4.69% in the trend window, so it is not worsening.
- **Usability:** 1,084 complaints [T007], severity sum 2,614 [T008], but mean severity is only 2.411439 [T009] and just 30 severe records [T010]. Note that this group includes ads. UI navigation alone scores 633 [C020].
- **Access:** only 151 complaints [T031] but mean severity 3.874172 [T033] and 131 severe records [T034]. Login failure is small in volume (118 [C025]) yet severe; a cheap targeted fix could run in parallel. It would rank higher if volume grows.

## Limitations

- Reviews are self-selected and public; there is no revenue, plan, or churn data, and cancellation language is intent only.
- Of 10,000 source rows, 9,999 were completed and 1 quarantined; 1,552 completed via exact text reuse and 1,661 were flagged needs-review, out of 4,462 complaint or cancellation records.
- Verifier agreement on a 200-review sample: topic 0.825, intent 0.865, exact severity 0.725 (MAE 0.33). Label noise is therefore real, especially for severity.
- The baseline score is count multiplied by severity, so it weights volume heavily. The "other" group (1,328 complaints [T001]) is unclassified and may hide actionable issues.
